chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Highlights of fourteen years: the one-night stands and the Europe trip
summary: Crawford says a job was a job, the band was the biggest one-nighter band, and the European trip was successful.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What would you -- could you describe some of the jobs that you feel were highlights?

Well, some of your -- some of the jobs when you worked with Lunsford, through the 14 years you were with Lunsford, what were some of the jobs that stood out most in your mind that you worked, other than the Cotton Club. You already told us about the Cotton Club.

Well, we didn't -- a job was a job. As I told you, just catching the booker, who would run off with the money -- now, I told you about that. We drove through a very rainy night to try to catch this booker, who was in his car, and Lunsford was right behind him.
Oh, yeah, you told us -- you told us about that.
What about the trip to Europe? How was that?
We had started -- we'd begun making records then. So we became quite popular over there, Scandinavia and various other countries. And I didn't miss --

we didn't miss a whistle stop in this country. I mean we played everything that -- [knew anything] in the dance hall, Lunceford played it. As I told you before, we were the biggest one nighter band in the land. Well, we didn't have no steady work of our own, so we had to do one nighters.
Well now, can you tell us about -- give us some details about the trip to Europe?
